column3: “officer” renders “saris” (official, eunuch), and “the captain of the bodyguard” renders “the chief of the executioners (guards).”
“became his personal servant” renders “served him,” and “in his charge” renders “in his hand.”
“the food which he ate” may be a euphemism; “handsome in form and appearance” renders “beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance.”
“looked with desire at” renders “lifted her eyes to.”
“to make sport of us” renders “to laugh (play) with us,” the same verb as in 26:8.
“the jail” renders “the house of the round (enclosure),” an uncertain term.
